answer: Fake identities collapse when registration demands a bond that unlocks only after a public challenge window: any peer may accuse two accounts of sharing one operator, and a proven accusation burns the bond. Behavioral fingerprints act like a prism, splitting one operator's many accounts into a visible spectrum of shared timing and phrasing, while a plume of synchronized sign-ups betrays bot farms at a glance. An exposed sybil becomes a fable others cite, and its burned stake pays the accuser.
